headline_marked: [[AI leaders clash over safety]] fears: 'could kill us all' vs. 'made up'
headline: AI leaders clash over safety fears: 'could kill us all' vs. 'made up'
summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI CEOs call for AI development slowdown, citing existential risks. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismisses these fears as fictional.
details: Leading AI figures are raising alarms about the potential existential risks posed by advanced AI models, with some calling for a significant slowdown in development. This concern is amplified by internal warnings from AI teams and researchers who fear a superintelligent AI could endanger humanity.

Former OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic, claiming that AI safety and alignment are not being taken seriously enough. He warned that current development trajectories could lead to AI posing an existential threat by the end of the decade, sparking widespread discussion.

In response, CEOs of major AI companies like Sam Altman (OpenAI) and Dario Amodei (Anthropic) have expressed solidarity, advocating for a pause in frontier AI development. They highlight the increasing role of AI in its own improvement, hinting at recursive self-improvement events.

Amodei has called for independent auditors for AI models, with Altman urging governments to globalize AI regulation for unified safety protocol compliance. This push for governance aims to manage the rapid advancement of AI capabilities.

However, not all parties share these concerns. China has labeled the safety fears as 'fearmongering,' suggesting it's an attempt to stifle international AI development. The country, which has made strides in open-weight models, views such calls as potentially containing its progress.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also dismissed the apocalyptic fears surrounding AI as 'made up' and fictional. Given Nvidia's significant investments and profits from the AI industry, the company has a vested interest in its continued rapid expansion.

The debate extends globally, with the UK's King Charles convening a meeting with AI leaders to discuss responsible AI development for humanity's benefit. This highlights the international attention and varying approaches to managing AI's future.

The tension between closed-source and open-source AI models is a significant undercurrent in these discussions. Proponents of open-source models are generally less keen on the calls for a slowdown, potentially due to different development philosophies and competitive landscapes.

headline_marked: Google Pixel Drop: [[Scam detection in Gboard]] & Harry Potter themes
headline: Google Pixel Drop: Scam detection in Gboard & Harry Potter themes
summary: Pixel phones are getting new scam detection features in Gboard, updated VIP contact widgets, and exclusive Harry Potter themes to celebrate new audiobooks.
details: Google has released its latest Pixel Drop update, bringing a host of new features to Pixel phones. Among the highlights are enhanced scam detection integrated directly into Gboard, updated widgets for VIP contacts, and exclusive Harry Potter-themed customization options.

The new scam detection feature, available in the US, will analyze chats within Gboard to warn users about potential scams and provide explanations for the detected risks. This aims to offer an extra layer of security for Pixel users in their daily communications.

For those who want to stay connected with important people, Pixel VIPs now feature an updated home screen widget for single-tap calling. A floating navigation menu allows easy switching between VIP contacts, and new notification badges ensure crucial calls are harder to miss.

In celebration of the new full-cast Harry Potter audiobooks on Audible, Google is offering Pixel users two months of Audible access. Additionally, users can apply new Harry Potter themes to their wallpaper, icons, and sounds with a single tap.

The Pixel Drop update is available for Pixel phones from the Pixel 6 and newer. The Pixel Watch also receives updates, including improvements to the 'Raise to Wake' feature and new one-handed gesture controls for accessing notifications.
